fields.description:
## Context / Problem

The platform verifies one artifact and publishes a different one, and nothing reconciles the two.

`_clean_checkout` at `services/orchestration/temporal_activities/checks.py:38` copies the workspace working tree and checks that copy, on the stated basis that it is "exactly what the pull request will carry". The publish path never reads the workspace. `collect_changes` at `services/orchestration/materialization.py:177` reduces it to a `dict[str, str]`, and `commit_and_push` at `adapters/real/git_host.py:120` clones into a temporary directory, writes those files, commits and pushes.

That mapping is lossy. It skips porcelain statuses containing `D` (line 185), so deletions never reach the branch. It reads paths with `read_text(encoding="utf-8")` (line 189), so binary files raise. It passes `--no-renames` (line 179), so a rename becomes an add plus a dropped delete. Modes are carried nowhere.

Three mechanisms then assume one commit per execution, which the CI repair loop violates. `mediator.py:115` targets its `SideEffectRef` on `f"{repo}:{request.branch}"`, and `side_effect_key` at `services/coordination/idempotency.py:39` hashes only task, execution, operation and target. All three git hosts return early on a prior `execution_id` trailer, at `adapters/real/git_host.py:127`, `adapters/real/local_git_host.py:124` and an `applied` set at `adapters/mock/git_host.py:98`. The activity at `services/orchestration/temporal_activities/pull_request.py:287` re-materializes at the previous push's head, so `_ensure_checkout` at `materialization.py:145` runs `reset --hard` and `clean -fd` over the first repair's edits.

Pilot execution `intake-83bd3367` pushed at sequences 202, 205 and 207, all returning commit `37fd44e7a7` against one ledger row. Its second repair fixed a snapshot file, checks passed, and the promoted branch lacks that fix and fails 6 tests in the platform's own image.

## Approach

Publish the workspace itself rather than a reconstruction of it.

The workspace is already a git checkout with an authenticated remote, because `materialization.py:88` takes `remote_url_for` from `build_git_host(resolved).source_location`, which `adapters/real/git_host.py:81` returns as the same URL the adapter pushes with. No new credentials are needed.

The workspace stages its change and the adapter commits that staged tree in the workspace and pushes the branch. The temporary clone and the file mapping go away, so deletions, renames, binary content and modes survive because git carries them.

Content addressing replaces the execution-scoped dedup. `git write-tree` yields a hash that differs per repair attempt and repeats for a retry of one attempt, which is the idempotency the trailer search was reaching for, without a counter. The adapter replays when the remote head's tree matches the staged tree, so a retry after a push that already landed is safe rather than a non-fast-forward rejection. That tree also becomes the `SideEffectRef` target.

Re-materialization then resolves itself, because the head the workflow carries forward becomes the workspace head and `_ensure_checkout` takes its early return at `materialization.py:151`. An arbitrary base still works, since the workspace is materialized once at the requested base and afterwards only moves forward by local commits. After pushing, the activity checks that the remote branch head equals the workspace head and that the workspace is clean, so a future divergence fails the run rather than promoting.

The commit disables signing and hooks for the reason ADEVX-130 established, since an inherited `commit.gpgsign` or a failing `pre-commit` hook produces no commit while reporting success. Keeping the mapping and adding a ledger discriminator was rejected, because the trailer search would still decline the push and the fidelity losses would remain.

## Scope

Per-file reasons are recorded in this ticket's file impact. `CommitRequest` swaps `files` for `workspace` and `tree`, all three git hosts commit from the workspace and drop their execution-keyed dedup, the materializer gains staging and loses `collect_changes`, the mediator targets the ledger on the tree, the activity stages and then verifies the push, and `bounded_task_pipeline` reads the no-changes outcome from staging. `tests/unit/test_commit_publish.py` is new, and the five existing suites named in the file impact move to the workspace contract.

## Grounded assumptions

- The workspace is a full checkout on the activity worker rather than in the sandbox, since `_clean_checkout` reads it with `shutil.copytree` and `materialization.py` runs `git` against it there.
- The agent's edits reach the workspace as a patch, so deletions are expressible there and the loss happens later, in `collect_changes`.
- `build_commit_request` at `materialization.py:199` is the only non-test caller of `collect_changes`.
- The sequence gate does not block the extra pushes. `_admissible` at `services/coordination/sequencing.py:30` admits a sequence ahead of the current one, and the pilot carried 202, 205 and 207.

## Testing

Unit tests cover publish fidelity for a deletion, a rename, binary content and a mode change, the two-commit repair loop, tree-based replay including a retry after a push that already landed, the no-change outcome, a signing and hook hostile repository, and both post-push verification failures. An integration test covers re-materialization preserving uncommitted edits, and a live pilot run covers the end-to-end path.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A deleted file is absent from the published tree and a renamed file appears only at its new path, verified by `tests/unit/test_commit_publish.py`.
- [ ] A binary file is published byte for byte rather than raising, verified by a test publishing bytes that are not valid UTF-8.
- [ ] A file made executable retains that mode, verified by a test reading `git ls-tree`.
- [ ] Two staged changes in one execution produce two distinct commits on the branch, the second descending from the first, verified by a test asserting the branch holds two commits.
- [ ] Publishing the same staged tree twice pushes once and reports `replayed` on the second call, and a publish retried after the remote already holds the tree replays rather than failing on a non-fast-forward, verified by two unit tests.
- [ ] Two different staged trees in one execution produce two different `SideEffectRef` targets, verified by a test over `services/integration/github/mediator.py`.
- [ ] A workspace with no staged difference yields the no-changes outcome and creates no commit, verified by a staging unit test and a `bounded_task_pipeline` test.
- [ ] A workspace configured with `commit.gpgsign` and a `pre-commit` hook exiting non-zero is still committed, verified by a test executing the publish against such a repository.
- [ ] A re-materialization at the head the previous push created preserves uncommitted workspace edits, verified by a test in `tests/integration/test_workspace_materialization.py`.
- [ ] The activity fails when the remote head does not equal the workspace head after pushing, and when the workspace is not clean after committing, verified by two unit tests.
- [ ] `collect_changes` is removed and no caller remains, verified by a repository-wide search returning no match.
- [ ] [non-codebase] A live run of the pilot ticket through at least one repair cycle promotes a pull request whose head passes the checks the platform reported.
  provenance: environment=local-colima-k3s; principal=joeoakhart; privilege_posture=production-equivalent; instrument=live-call — the pilot executes the shipped workflow against the client repository over the same Temporal path a deployment uses
- [ ] `ruff check services tests scripts adapters` exits 0 and the full unit and integration suite passes.
